title: A Stranger at the Gate
text: A stranger in a good coat has come to the gate. He says he is a steward of the Tollmaster's men, that the store is owed a tithe, and that he would like to be let in to count it.

choices.label: Go down and talk him out of it

success.chronicle: {When}, the abbot went down to the gate and talked the steward into a smaller count, and went back up with the store untouched.

failure.chronicle: {When}, the steward would not be talked out of anything, and took a basket of bread for his masters before he rode off.

choices.label: Keep the gate shut
choices.chronicle: {When}, the gate stayed shut, and the steward rode off to tell his masters so.

title: A Stag in the Glen
text: The snow came early, and the kitchen has counted the sacks twice. {monk} says there is a stag in the glen, if someone can get close enough to it.

success.chronicle: {When}, {monk} came back at dusk with a stag over his shoulders, and the kitchen had meat for a month.

failure.chronicle: {When}, {monk} came back from the glen with nothing but a cut hand from the rocks.

choices.label: Let the stag be
choices.chronicle: {When}, the stag was left in the glen, and the brothers ate their bread and were grateful for it.
